visibility_dispatch.head: push esi; push edi; mov esi,ecx; xor edi,edi; call 0x0042B820; mov eax,[esp+0xC]; cmp eax,0xF; ja 0x0042B3DD; jmp [eax*4+0x0042B3E4]
visibility_dispatch.return_contract: eax = edi: 1 = target was OPENED (was hidden); 0 = target was CLOSED or id invalid (ids 5/10 and >0xF jump straight to the shared tail 0x42B3DD with edi=0 from the prologue xor). Callers rely on this: Q/W/E/R/S/D/N/G letters, Enter case1, FnB 0x43E4B0 notice path, caption action stubs (cap14 toggles only when return 0, cap15 double-toggle gates on return).
visibility_dispatch.close_all: 0x0042B820 demote-all runs before the case: walks the visible list from [base+0xD28] head via node+4 (prev links), resets [base+0xD34]=0 and per listed node id <= 0xE executes table 0x42B938 -> 0x423F90(subwin, 0) (mov [subwin+0x34],0; ret 4); ids 5/10 -> 0x42B8F5 no-op advance, id > 0xE skipped; loop inc edi / cmp edi,[base+0xD38] / jl. This is DEACTIVATION of the +0x34 slot only - it does NOT touch the +0x30 visibility gate and does NOT unlink list nodes. 3 E8 callers: 0x42ADB6 (dispatcher head), 0x42B6B3 (drag-start 0x42B6A0), 0x42BD8F (FnA hit-test fallback).
visibility_dispatch.case_pattern: mov eax,[esi+flagoff]; push id; test eax,eax; mov ecx,esi; je OPEN; call 0x0042AC50; vtable[0x10](0); xor edi,edi; ret | OPEN: call 0x0042AC30; vtable[0x10](1); [per-id specials]; mov edi,1; ret. flagoff = objectoff + 0x30 in every case (see records).
